verdicts.note: Explicit and repeated: 'less taxation' in the voters' guide [S1], 'Lower Taxes' and lower tax burdens on local entrepreneurs on her home and platform pages [S2][S3]. Two independent documents (pamphlet and campaign site) and no pole-b statement anywhere in the dossier, so -2 at high holds.

'Stop wasteful spending', regular department audits and accounting for 'every penny' [S1][S3] are the audit-and-restrain pole almost word for word, and she says the county must 'live within its means' with a line-by-line review [S4]. The one hedge, 'not to make cuts just for the sake of cutting' [S4], qualifies how she would cut, not whether she leans toward restraint. Three sources; -2 high stands.

Affordability through cutting 'regulations, fees and permitting delays', 'pro-growth policies' and rural development [S4][S3], plus a comprehensive plan that 'should not become another layer of red tape' [S4]. No public-housing or tenant-protection position in the dossier. -2 is the strong end, but every piece of evidence is deregulatory; medium fits one Q&A and one platform page.

Attacked on single-source strength: the only evidence is platform bullets on one page, 'fully fund law enforcement' and 'strong and real consequences for violence and theft', plus opposing state mandates that 'undermine local policing efforts' [S3]. The attack fails on direction and balance: all are enforcement-pole statements and nothing in the dossier points to prevention or diversion. Medium already reflects the single source.

Direction holds: she has never held county or other government office and is challenging the sitting commission chair [S1][S5]. Two parts of the basis are unsupported. 'First run for public office' is wrong as stated: the dossier says first run for county office, and she has served as a precinct committee officer and state committeewoman and chairs the county Republican Party [S1][S5]. The 'status quo' quote does not appear anywhere in her dossier. Her profile is a party-establishment figure rather than an outsider or generational-change candidate, and the dossier records no explicit 'new voices' pitch from her, so +2 at high overstates it.

Term limits for county officials, a ban on lobbying by former county officials, limits on executive sessions and a salary commission [S1][S3] are reform-pole items (term limits are named in pole_b). Not +2: no PAC-money refusal or election-system reform, and she runs as county party chair with party and legislator endorsements [S2]. +1 medium is right.
Four-year incumbent, board chair since 2024, running on his record [S1][S3], elected in 2022 [S5]. Two independent sources; -2 high stands.

Tried to push it to 0: the evidence is balanced budgets with 'core services ... preserved' and new grant, fee and interest revenue [S2], which is maintenance rather than an audit agenda, and the scorer's own basis says 'no cut or expansion agenda'. It survives at -1 because his budget answer is about keeping departments off the general fund [S2] and he wants the state 'to control spending' [S2]; nothing points toward expansion. Medium is the ceiling.

'A builder by trade', he says housing costs 'have always been driven by supply and demand' and points to permitting reform in the comprehensive plan [S2]. He also lists affordable housing among the county's work [S2], which keeps this at -1 rather than -2.

The only cited evidence is one sentence about 'tax reform' needing the state 'to control spending and not rely on us, the citizens, to bridge the gap' [S2]. That is about state spending, and 'tax reform' is not defined. The scorer missed S10, which muddies it: in a March 2026 story on the county considering taxing timberland owners, he said 'it's time for the county to revisit the rates' [S10], and the dossier notes the direction is not stated. The dossier's own scoring note says 'No explicit position on local tax levels' [S2][S10]. The direction is plausible but too thin for medium.
